Position Summary:

***’s Warehouse Associates are individual contributors responsible for executing warehousing activities for incoming and outgoing goods. Warehouse associates receive, handle, store, record and dispatch goods in the warehouse. Ensures various warehousing operations including packing and storage, replenishment, picking, loading and dispatching are executed in a safe, timely and efficient manner. Maintains complete and accurate data in the ERP (SxE) system.

Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities:

• Completes shipments by processing and loading orders; reads production schedule, customer order, work order, shipping order, or requisition to determine items to be moved, gathered, or distributed.
• Unloads, receives and puts away incoming goods and merchandise; unpacks bales, crates, and other containers; checks for damage and for discrepancies between goods and invoices; may install strapping, bracing, or padding to prevent shifting or damage in transit from truck to warehouse and/or shelving.
• Accurately sorts, labels, moves and stores goods and merchandise; places material or items on racks, shelves, or in bins according to predetermined sequence such as size, style, or product codes; arranges storage to optimize warehouse space; reads work orders or follows verbal instructions to ascertain materials or containers to be moved.

• Complies tickets or worksheets from customer specifications.
• Operates warehouse equipment as needed to complete tasks (e.g., forklifts, cherry-picking lifts, pallet jacks, or other warehouse machinery).
• Assists in inventory level maintenance and inventory counts.
• Responsible for following warehouse safety regulations.
• Performs other duties as assigned.

1+ year of relevant experience and/or training. High school diploma or equivalent preferred (not required).
Relevant experience and/or aptitude should include:
• Demonstration of attention to detail, safety minded.
• Loading, unloading, picking, packing or moving goods in a warehouse environment; forklift / cherry picker experience preferred.
• Demonstrated ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, work orders, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.
• Basic computer knowledge and proficiency and/or a demonstrated technical aptitude to learn; preferred technical skills to include but not limited to MS-Office products, Vista, Control, SX.e, Prophet 21.
• Demonstration of basic mathematical skills (add, subtract, multiply and divide in all units to measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals); ability to compute rate*** ratio, and percent preferred.
• Ability to compile routine reports and write correspondence.
• Ability to work in a team environment and be self-motivated to accomplish assigned tasks and goals.

• Assigned work shifts may vary and/or rotate.
• Overtime may be required; extended day, evening and weekend work may be required as job duties demand and may include little to no advanced notice.
• Must be able to handle and work physical inventory; required to lift up to 50 lbs or greater with assistance following standard operating and safety procedures. Other physical requirements including, regularly being required to stand, walk, kneel, bend, crouch, crawl, climb and balance.

title: Calibration Technician
description:
Overview

Our client is a dynamic, innovative, and growing leader in calibration and compliance services across North America. With over 1,000 employees in technical, consulting, operational, sales, finance, and corporate roles, they support vital industries including life sciences, aerospace, defense, energy, and utilities.

Employees are at the center of the rewarding, challenging, and impactful work being done for customers and the industries they serve. This is an excellent opportunity to join a company where your work makes a difference, and where you’ll be supported with training, career growth, and competitive benefits.

What’s Offered

  • Work that matters.

  • A values-driven culture where teamwork and respect are central.

  • Flexibility and career development opportunities.

  • Training and professional development to accelerate growth.

  • Competitive compensation and benefits, including paid time off, health insurance, tuition reimbursement, retirement plans, and more.

Summary

The Field Calibration Technician will provide on-site calibration of test equipment for customers within the assigned region (typically within an 8-hour radius). When not traveling, this role will also support the local calibration laboratory. This is a travel-based position, requiring Monday–Friday availability with overnight stays; technicians are typically home on weekends. All lodging and travel expenses are company-paid.

Responsibilities

Major Areas of Responsibility

  • Calibrate measurement and test equipment (M&TE) to manufacturer specifications.

  • Identify and document out-of-tolerance conditions for customer M&TE and calibration standards.

  • Perform corrective actions, such as adjustments or minor repairs, when equipment is out of tolerance.

  • Accurately update and maintain calibration documentation and service records.

  • Provide feedback and recommendations on calibration practices and procedures.

  • Maintain calibration standards in compliance with quality requirements.

  • Communicate effectively with customers regarding services and equipment needs.

  • Submit and update all required paperwork for travel and administrative purposes.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Travel Requirements

  • Travel Monday–Friday to customer facilities.

  • Overnight travel required during the week (company-paid lodging and expenses).

  • Home on weekends 95% of the time.

Qualifications

Required Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Calibration experience and/or equivalent training with commercial and/or biomedical M&TE.

  • Strong self-motivation with the ability to work independently.

  • Excellent customer service skills with professional communication.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, internet tools, and basic database functionality.

  • Valid driver’s license with 3+ years of driving experience and an acceptable driving record.

Education & Experience

  • Associate degree in a technical field; OR 2–5 years of relevant calibration experience/training; OR equivalent combination of education and experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Military PMEL training.

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to follow written procedures.

  • Excellent organizational skills, with the ability to plan and prioritize workloads.

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.

Physical Demands

  • Ability to stand for long periods (up to 8 hours/day).

  • Frequent use of hands and fingers to handle tools and equipment.

  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly and occasionally up to 75 lbs.

  • Ability to maneuver a 400-pound cart from unloading area to service area.

  • Occasional walking, reaching, climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, or crawling.

  • Reasonable accommodations will be made for individuals with disabilities.

Work Environment

  • Regular exposure to risks of electrical shock.

  • Frequent exposure to moving mechanical parts.

  • Occasional exposure to wet/humid conditions, heights, airborne particles, chemicals, outdoor weather, and vibration.

  • Noise level is typically moderate.

title: Director – Rates & Regulatory Affairs
description:
Director – Rates & Regulatory Affairs

Location: Phoenix, AZ
Position Type: Full Time
Education Level: Bachelor's Degree
Job Category: Management

Description

We are seeking an experienced Director – Rates & Regulatory Affairs to lead regulatory filings, rate cases, and compliance initiatives. Reporting to executive leadership, this role plays a critical part in shaping and executing regulatory strategy, managing key regulatory initiatives, and ensuring compliance while supporting overall business goals. The ideal candidate will have extensive utility regulatory experience, strong analytical skills, and the ability to translate regulatory outcomes into actionable business strategies that maximize rate recovery and support long-term growth.

Essential Duties

  • Coordinate the preparation, submission, and management of regulatory applications, filings, and rate cases.

  • Develop ratemaking models and prepare filings for rate surcharges, adjustors, and similar mechanisms.

  • Identify and implement improvements to ratemaking processes, modeling, and planning activities.

  • Ensure compliance with regulatory decisions, directives, and industry requirements.

  • Lead tariff management, revenue/sales reporting, and compliance tracking.

  • Prepare and summarize financial information for budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning.

  • Conduct economic and cost/benefit analyses for projects, acquisitions, and feasibility studies.

  • Develop industry-related studies, including customer growth, usage, and statistical benchmarking.

  • Provide timely updates on regulatory rules, regulations, and emerging practices.

  • Perform research projects and special assignments on regulatory, operational, and management matters.

Skills, Knowledge & Requirements

  • Strong background in finance, accounting, economics, and statistics.

  • Advanced understanding of revenue requirements, cost recovery mechanisms, and ratemaking principles.

  • Prior experience working with state public utility commissions strongly preferred.

  • Strong business acumen and ability to link regulatory decisions to utility operations, financial performance, and strategy.

  • Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (advanced level).

  • Comfortable working as both a leader and individual contributor in a fast-paced environment.

  • Ability to perform physical activities typical of an office environment, including lifting up to 40 pounds.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or related field from an accredited college or university.

  • 10+ years of prior experience with a public utility in rates, regulatory affairs, or accounting.
